All done. The kernel compiles and passes correctness (5/5 trials) on gfx942 (MI300X).

The implementation uses four AveLang kernels:

1. **`conv2d_3x3_kernel`** — direct 3×3 convolution with FP32 accumulation, each thread computes one output element via the full 8×3×3 inner loop
2. **`group_norm_stats_kernel`** — per-(sample, group) reduction computing sum and sum-of-squares into FP32 buffers, using shared memory to aggregate per-thread partials (thread 0 sums, no while loop needed)
3. **`group_norm_apply_tanh_hardswish_kernel`** — reads the precomputed stats, applies GroupNorm with learnable gamma/beta, then `al.tanh` and a custom HardSwish (using if/else for float min/max since `al.min`/`al.max` are integer-only)
4. **`residual_logsumexp_kernel`** — adds the conv residual to the processed output, then computes logsumexp over the channel dimension with the standard max-subtraction trick for numerical stability

Runtime is 5.56 ms vs 3.41 ms reference (~1.6×). The gap is expected — this is a direct convolution with no im2col+MFMA tiling, just basic correctness-first implementation. There is headroom for fused tiling and MFMA-based conv if you want to push it further.
